basis: Brain malformations, intellectual disability and ocular coloboma define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 5/6 patients.
Defined by developmental delay, intellectual disability and other neurodevelopmental abnormalities.
West Nile viral encephalitis; CNS infection defines this concept despite the definition also describing non-neuroinvasive infection.
Autoimmune thyroid-associated orbital disease; associated thyroid dysfunction is a separate endocrine condition.
Cerebellar degeneration with cognitive and pyramidal dysfunction; nystagmus reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Occlusion of a retinal artery directly affects the retinal circulation and eye.
Autonomic baroreflex dysfunction defined by severe blood-pressure fluctuations, including hypertension.
Presynaptic NMJ disorder; fixed congenital joint contractures occur in 2/5. Ptosis, weakness and hypoventilation reflect NMJ dysfunction.
Polyvalvular heart disease is the defining parent; the supplied record does not establish other common organ damage.
Isolated hereditary sensorineural hearing loss.
Immune-mediated lichen sclerosus causes genital skin atrophy and scarring; urethral involvement is a minority complication.
Congenital valve and pulmonary artery malformation; bronchial compression with airway dysfunction is common, approximately 30% or more.
Patellar defects and microtia define syndrome; neutropenia 5/6 with infections 5/7 supports immune deficiency. Mild intellectual disability omitted at cap.
Inherited encephalopathy with myelin vacuolization and seizures in 9/9; no established infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Inherited isolated nail dysplasia and dystrophy; rare autoimmune associations do not establish an immune mechanism.
Tertiary treponemal infection defined by destructive lesions of skin, bones and joints.
Splenic tissue necrosis caused by failure or obstruction of its arterial or venous blood supply.
Chronic erosive injury of gastric mucosa; no specific infectious or autoimmune cause is established.
Dermatophyte infection of groin and perianal skin; intestinal mucosa is not involved.
Defined here as a benign nerve-sheath neoplasm; typically arises within the dermis or subcutis as a cutaneous nodule.
Benign adipose neoplasm arising within the wall of the colon or rectum.
Myeloid blast neoplasm of marrow and blood; gingival infiltration is not established in at least 30% and is not a diagnostic criterion.
Inherited keratin disorder causing skin fragility, superficial blistering, erosions and ichthyosis.
Gas-filled cysts within the intestinal wall; no additional organ involvement is intrinsic to this concept.
Neonatal diabetes, skeletal dysplasia and recurrent liver failure define WRS; neutropenia occurs in 30-79%. Renal and neurologic involvement is below 30%.
